title: The condensed ring of continuous maps
statement:
Let $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$ be the category of profinite sets with the coherent topology, and
let $T$ be a topological ring. The presheaf of rings

$$
\underline T(S):=C(S,T),\qquad \underline T(S)\to\underline T(S'),\ a\mapsto a\circ u
\quad(u\colon S'\to S),
$$

with the pointwise ring operations, is a sheaf of rings on $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$. This is
the condensed ring $\underline T$. Its underlying abelian sheaf, with the ring object
structure of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], is a ring object of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$,
and this ring object is commutative when $T$ is.

proof.text: Put $P(S)=C(S,T)$. Addition and multiplication of continuous functions are continuous by composing $S\to T\times T$, $s\mapsto(a(s),b(s))$, with the continuous addition and multiplication of $T$; negation is composition with continuous negation, and the constant zero and one functions are continuous. All ring identities hold after evaluation at each $s\in S$. Precomposition preserves these operations, since $(a+b)\circ u=(a\circ u)+(b\circ u)$ and $(ab)\circ u=(a\circ u)(b\circ u)$, and preserves zero and one. The identities $a\circ\mathrm{id}=a$ and $(a\circ u)\circ v=a\circ(u\circ v)$ give the presheaf laws. This constructs the presheaf of unital rings directly, for noncommutative $T$ as well.

source.place: First paragraph: pointwise ring structure and precomposition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-coherent-sheaf-criterion] with $\mathcal A$ the category of unital rings. It suffices to check that $P$ takes finite disjoint coproducts to products of rings and that the kernel-pair diagram for every continuous surjection is an equalizer of rings. This uses the ring-valued version of the criterion directly.

For a finite family $(S_i)$, restriction gives $C(\coprod_iS_i,T)\to\prod_i C(S_i,T)$. Its inverse sends $(a_i)$ to the function $a(i,s)=a_i(s)$. For every open $V\subseteq T$, its inverse image is $\bigcup_i\{i\}\times a_i^{-1}(V)$, open in the disjoint union, so the inverse function is continuous. Both directions preserve every ring operation by evaluation on each component. Thus this is the product of rings, including the empty family: $C(\varnothing,T)$ is the one-element ring, terminal among unital rings.

source.place: Paragraph checking (a): maps out of a finite disjoint union.

proof.text: Let $q:S'\to S$ be a continuous surjection and let $b\in C(S',T)$ have equal pullbacks along both projections from $S'\times_S S'$. For $x,y$ with $q(x)=q(y)$ the pair $(x,y)$ lies in that fibre product, so $b(x)=b(y)$. Define $a(s)$ to be this common value on the nonempty fibre $q^{-1}(s)$. Then $a\circ q=b$, and surjectivity gives uniqueness. The source $S'$ is compact and the target $S$ is Hausdorff, so [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient] applies to $q$ with both spaces regarded as whole subspaces of themselves. For any open $V\subseteq T$, $q^{-1}(a^{-1}(V))=b^{-1}(V)$ is open; the quoted quotient criterion makes $a^{-1}(V)$ open. Hence $a$ is continuous. No Hausdorffness or completeness of $T$ is used.

source.place: Paragraph checking (b): fibrewise descent and continuity of the descended map.

proof.text: The equalizer assertion holds in rings, not just on elements. Given any unital ring $R$ and ring homomorphism $h:R\to C(S',T)$ whose two pullbacks agree, apply the preceding descent to $h(r)$ for each $r$ to obtain $\widetilde h(r)\in C(S,T)$. Evaluating at a lift $x$ of $s$ gives $\widetilde h(r+r')(s)=h(r+r')(x)=h(r)(x)+h(r')(x)$ and $\widetilde h(rr')(s)=h(r)(x)h(r')(x)$; $\widetilde h(0)(s)=h(0)(x)=0$ and $\widetilde h(1)(s)=h(1)(x)=1$. Thus $\widetilde h$ is a ring homomorphism with $q^*\widetilde h=h$. Surjectivity of $q$ makes it the unique such homomorphism. This is the equalizer universal property. Together with the finite product calculation, [lem-sfb-profinite-coherent-sheaf-criterion] now proves that $P$ is a sheaf of rings. Define $\underline T$ to be this sheaf with the already constructed sections and restrictions.

source.place: Conditions (a), (b), with the first paragraph reduction replaced by the explicit ring-valued universal property.

proof.text: Use the tensor and size convention in the current statement of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]: abelian sheaves have the sheafified objectwise tensor product over $\mathbf Z$ with unit $a(\underline{\mathbf Z})$, on an essentially small site. Fix the universe of the profinite sets and take a larger ambient universe for the sheaf categories, so that this site is essentially small there; the cited statement explicitly includes the coherent site of profinite sets. Its part 3 says that the underlying abelian sheaf of any sheaf of rings on this site is a ring object for this tensor product, commutative when all its section rings are. Apply it to the sheaf $\underline T$ constructed in steps 1–5. If $T$ is commutative, $(ab)(s)=a(s)b(s)=b(s)a(s)=(ba)(s)$ for every $s$, so every $C(S,T)$ is commutative and the ring object is commutative.

source.place: Last paragraph: part 3 of the ring-object construction and commutativity.
